tools.name: CronCreate
tools.description:
Schedule a prompt to be enqueued at a future time. Use for both recurring schedules and one-shot reminders.

Uses standard 5-field cron in the user's local timezone: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week. "0 9 * * *" means 9am local — no timezone conversion needed.

## One-shot tasks (recurring: false)

For "remind me at X" or "at <time>, do Y" requests — fire once then auto-delete.
Pin minute/hour/day-of-month/month to specific values:
  "remind me at 2:30pm today to check the deploy" → cron: "30 14 <today_dom> <today_month> *", recurring: false
  "tomorrow morning, run the smoke test" → cron: "57 8 <tomorrow_dom> <tomorrow_month> *", recurring: false

## Recurring jobs (recurring: true, the default)

For "every N minutes" / "every hour" / "weekdays at 9am" requests:
  "*/5 * * * *" (every 5 min), "0 * * * *" (hourly), "0 9 * * 1-5" (weekdays at 9am local)

## Avoid the :00 and :30 minute marks when the task allows it

Every user who asks for "9am" gets `0 9`, and every user who asks for "hourly" gets `0 *` — which means requests from across the planet land on the API at the same instant. When the user's request is approximate, pick a minute that is NOT 0 or 30:
  "every morning around 9" → "57 8 * * *" or "3 9 * * *" (not "0 9 * * *")
  "hourly" → "7 * * * *" (not "0 * * * *")
  "in an hour or so, remind me to..." → pick whatever minute you land on, don't round

Only use minute 0 or 30 when the user names that exact time and clearly means it ("at 9:00 sharp", "at half past", coordinating with a meeting). When in doubt, nudge a few minutes early or late — the user will not notice, and the fleet will.

## Durability

By default (durable: false) the job lives only in this Claude session — nothing is written to disk, and the job is gone when Claude exits. Pass durable: true to write to .claude/scheduled_tasks.json so the job survives restarts. Only use durable: true when the user explicitly asks for the task to persist ("keep doing this every day", "set this up permanently"). Most "remind me in 5 minutes" / "check back in an hour" requests should stay session-only.

## Runtime behavior

Jobs only fire while the REPL is idle (not mid-query). Durable jobs persist to .claude/scheduled_tasks.json and survive session restarts — on next launch they resume automatically. One-shot durable tasks that were missed while the REPL was closed are surfaced for catch-up. Session-only jobs die with the process. The scheduler shifts each job by a fixed per-job offset on top of whatever you pick: by default a recurring job runs up to 50% of its period late (max 30 min), and a one-shot job landing on :00 or :30 runs up to 90 s early. The result of this tool and of CronList gives each job's actual next run time: when you tell the user when a job will run, give that time, not the minute in the cron expression. Picking an off-minute is still the bigger lever.

Recurring tasks auto-expire after 7 days — they fire one final time, then are deleted. This bounds session lifetime. Tell the user about the 7-day limit when scheduling recurring jobs.

Returns a job ID you can pass to CronDelete.

tools.name: EnterWorktree
tools.description:
Use this tool ONLY when explicitly instructed to work in a worktree — either by the user directly, or by project instructions (CLAUDE.md / memory). This tool creates an isolated git worktree and switches the current session into it.

## When to Use

- The user explicitly says "worktree" (e.g., "start a worktree", "work in a worktree", "create a worktree", "use a worktree")
- CLAUDE.md or memory instructions direct you to work in a worktree for the current task

## When NOT to Use

- The user asks to create a branch, switch branches, or work on a different branch — use git commands instead
- The user asks to fix a bug or work on a feature — use normal git workflow unless worktrees are explicitly requested by the user or project instructions
- Never use this tool unless "worktree" is explicitly mentioned by the user or in CLAUDE.md / memory instructions

## Requirements

- Must be in a git repository, OR have WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove hooks configured in settings.json
- Must not already be in a worktree session when creating a new worktree (`name`); switching into another existing worktree via `path` is allowed

## Behavior

- In a git repository: creates a new git worktree inside `.claude/worktrees/` on a new branch. The base ref is governed by the `worktree.baseRef` setting: `fresh` (default) branches from origin/<default-branch>; `head` branches from your current local HEAD
- Outside a git repository: delegates to WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove hooks for VCS-agnostic isolation
- Switches the session's working directory to the new worktree
- Use ExitWorktree to leave the worktree mid-session (keep or remove). On session exit, if still in the worktree, the user will be prompted to keep or remove it

## Entering an existing worktree

Pass `path` instead of `name` to switch the session into a worktree that already exists (e.g., one you just created with `git worktree add`). On first entry from the launch directory, the path must appear in `git worktree list` for the repository that owns it — the current repository or, in a multi-repo workspace, a repository nested inside it; paths registered by neither are rejected. ExitWorktree will not remove a worktree entered this way; use `action: "keep"` to return to the original directory.

Switching with `path` also works when the session is already in a worktree (the previous worktree is left on disk, untouched, and only the new one is tracked for exit-time cleanup), and from agents whose working directory was pinned at launch (subagent isolation or explicit cwd). In both cases the target must be a worktree under `.claude/worktrees/` of the same repository, and from a pinned agent the switch only affects this agent, not the parent session. After a further switch, previously-visited worktrees are no longer writable — re-issue EnterWorktree with `path` to return to one.

## Parameters

- `name` (optional): A name for a new worktree. If neither `name` nor `path` is provided, a random name is generated.
- `path` (optional): Path to an existing worktree to enter instead of creating one — of the current repository, or (on first entry from the launch directory) of a repository nested inside it. Mutually exclusive with `name`.

name.description: Optional name for a new worktree. Each "/"-separated segment may contain only letters, digits, dots, underscores, and dashes; max 64 chars total. A random name is generated if not provided. Mutually exclusive with `path`.

path.description: Path to an existing worktree to switch into instead of creating a new one. Must appear in `git worktree list` for the current repo — or, on first entry from the launch directory, for a repo nested inside it (multi-repo workspace). Mutually exclusive with `name`.

tools.name: ExitWorktree
tools.description:
Exit a worktree session created by EnterWorktree and return the session to the original working directory.

## Scope

This tool ONLY operates on worktrees created by EnterWorktree in this session. It will NOT touch:
- Worktrees you created manually with `git worktree add`
- Worktrees from a previous session (even if created by EnterWorktree then)
- The directory you're in if EnterWorktree was never called

If called outside an EnterWorktree session, the tool is a **no-op**: it reports that no worktree session is active and takes no action. Filesystem state is unchanged.

## When to Use

- The user explicitly asks to "exit the worktree", "leave the worktree", "go back", or otherwise end the worktree session
- Do NOT call this proactively — only when the user asks

## Parameters

- `action` (required): `"keep"` or `"remove"`
  - `"keep"` — leave the worktree directory and branch intact on disk. Use this if the user wants to come back to the work later, or if there are changes to preserve.
  - `"remove"` — delete the worktree directory and its branch. Use this for a clean exit when the work is done or abandoned.
- `discard_changes` (optional, default false): only meaningful with `action: "remove"`. If the worktree has uncommitted files or commits not on the original branch, the tool will REFUSE to remove it unless this is set to `true`. If the tool returns an error listing changes, confirm with the user before re-invoking with `discard_changes: true`.

## Behavior

- Restores the session's working directory to where it was before EnterWorktree
- Clears CWD-dependent caches (system prompt sections, memory files, plans directory) so the session state reflects the original directory
- If a tmux session was attached to the worktree: killed on `remove`, left running on `keep` (its name is returned so the user can reattach)
- Once exited, EnterWorktree can be called again to create a fresh worktree

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: SendMessage
tools.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

to.description: Recipient: a name from ListAgents (append its " [ref]" only when a listing or an error shows one), a teammate name, "main", or a background agent's agentId

summary.description: A 5-10 word label for your own transcript row (not transmitted — the recipient previews the first line of `message`). Truncated to 200 characters rather than rejected.

message.description: Plain text message content. The recipient's human sees only the FIRST LINE as a one-line preview until they expand it, so make the first line a clear, self-contained sentence saying what this is about — not a greeting, preamble, or bare @-mention.

notify_when_idle.description: Ask a session ON THIS MACHINE to send you ONE notice when it next goes idle (finishes its turn with nothing queued) or exits — opt-in, one-shot, no polling. With a message: deliver it now AND subscribe. Without a message (omit it): a pure subscription that costs the other session nothing.

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

plan.description: Replacement ExecutablePlan (kind executable); the proposal's requirement and evidence references are kept. Schema: testmaster://schemas/ExecutablePlan (steps: testmaster://schemas/Step)

expectedVersion.description: Proposal version being edited, for optimistic concurrency

tools.name: mcp__testmaster__testmaster_explore
tools.description: Browser exploration of features (featureIds from testmaster://projects/{projectId}/features?match=) within a budget; provider/model pick the model; a model call is never cut.

featureIds.description: Feature ids to explore, looked up by stable key at testmaster://projects/{projectId}/features; empty with jobId resumes that job

budget.description: Exploration envelope: browser steps and time

provider.description: Model provider id for action resolution; absent: first allowed provider

model.description: Model id for action resolution; absent: the provider's first capable model

mutationActions.description: Approved form steps (plan Step objects: click, fill, press, select, check, uncheck; each with a locator) the controller may select when one matches an observed control; max 20, refused in production environments. Without it a form-only page offers the model nothing to choose

jobId.description: Existing exploration job to resume or retry

wait.description: Block until the job ends instead of returning its id

tools.name: mcp__testmaster__testmaster_generate_plan
tools.description: Generate plan proposals (not tests) from the approved snapshot (sourceSnapshotId); provider/model pick the model. Add secrets, auth profiles and API specs first. Proposals: testmaster://plan-batches/{batchId}.

sourceSnapshotId.description: Current fingerprint of the approved requirement snapshot (testmaster_review_requirements returns it; also at testmaster://requirements/{projectId})

type.description: Kind of tests to propose; auto lets the model choose per requirement

requirementIds.description: Restrict the plan to these requirements

provider.description: Model provider id for plan generation; absent: first allowed provider

model.description: Model id from the project's profiles; absent: the provider's first capable model

partialGeneration.description: After the repairs, store the proposals that pass the checks and list the refused ones in extensions['testmaster:refusedProposals']; default false: one refused proposal refuses the whole batch

tools.name: mcp__testmaster__testmaster_generate_tests
tools.description: Generate code candidates from accepted proposals (proposalIds) or revisions (revisionIds), or repair the candidate of a failed run (runId). Each candidate: id (its revision), testId, testName, code URI. Refused: validationErrors.

proposalIds.description: Accepted proposals to generate code for; give proposalIds or revisionIds (at least one), all from one project

revisionIds.description: Existing revisions to regenerate code for; give proposalIds or revisionIds (at least one), all from one project

runId.description: A completed, failed run of a code candidate: repairs that candidate from the run's failed steps. Exclusive with proposalIds and revisionIds

provider.description: Model provider id for code generation; absent: first allowed provider

model.description: Model id for code generation, validated before any call; absent: the provider's first structured-output model

tools.name: mcp__testmaster__testmaster_get_analysis
tools.description: Read the stored analysis without recomputing. NOT_FOUND if never requested; then call testmaster_analyze_run.

tools.name: mcp__testmaster__testmaster_get_evidence
tools.description: Page the evidence manifest (screenshots, DOM, console, network, logs) with resource links; check integrity and freshness, follow nextCursor; failedOnly narrows. Next: testmaster_analyze_run.

attemptId.description: Attempt; defaults to the last one

tools.name: mcp__testmaster__testmaster_get_run
tools.description: Get phase, outcome, gate, analysisStatus and the run's test, revision, environment and origin. Summary only: before naming a cause, call testmaster_get_evidence then testmaster_analyze_run.

timeoutMs.description: Wait deadline in ms; the run continues after it

tools.name: mcp__testmaster__testmaster_import_code
tools.description: Import Playwright (.ts) or pytest (.py) code as a new test (projectId) or a candidate code revision of a test (testId), checked like `test import`. A candidate needs a passing replay, then promotion.

path.description: Entry file (.ts Playwright or .py pytest) inside an approved root and the project root; its relative imports are bundled

projectId.description: Create a new test in this project; give projectId or testId

testId.description: Add the code as a candidate revision of this existing test instead; it is not active until testmaster_promote_revision

parentRevisionId.description: Parent of the candidate; only with testId (default: the test's active revision)

name.description: Name of a new test; default: the first test title in the code

tools.name: mcp__testmaster__testmaster_normalize_requirements
tools.description: Normalize source revisions into requirements (each with a status) and conflicts; returns sourceSnapshotId and version. Slow: _meta.progressToken notifies. Next: testmaster_review_requirements.

provider.description: Model provider id; absent: the first allowed provider with a capable model

model.description: Model id from the project's profiles; defaults to the first capable one

tools.name: mcp__testmaster__testmaster_open_report
tools.description: Locate a committed report of a run (runId) or a run_tests batch (batchId): location, format URIs and sizes in bytes. A read is one page: read offset=0, then add the page's bytes, until sizes[format]; concatenate before parsing.

runId.description: Run id; send runId or batchId

batchId.description: Batch id (the batchId/jobId of a run_tests receipt): one report over its member runs; send runId or batchId

tools.name: mcp__testmaster__testmaster_promote_revision
tools.description: Make a candidate revision active at expectedVersion (testVersion of testmaster://tests/{id}/revisions); an optional reason is recorded. A generated candidate needs a passing replay first; healed: testmaster_approve_healing.

revisionId.description: Candidate revision to make the active one of its test

expectedVersion.description: Current version of the test: testVersion of testmaster://tests/{id}/revisions, or version of testmaster://tests/{id}

reason.description: Why you promote; recorded on the test with the reviewer and time (test history shows it)

tools.name: mcp__testmaster__testmaster_propose_healing
tools.description: Propose a candidate changing only the locator of a failed action step of the active plan revision; assertions are never healed. abstained = no safe repair. Next: testmaster_review_healing.

tools.name: mcp__testmaster__testmaster_reject_healing
tools.description: Reject a reviewed healing proposal with a required reason, recorded with the reviewer and time; nothing is applied. Write scope; audited.

reason.description: Why you reject; recorded on the proposal with the reviewer and time (testmaster_review_healing shows it)

tools.name: mcp__testmaster__testmaster_review_healing
tools.description: Read a healing proposal: status, diff, risk, preservedAssertions.intact, verification and approval. Next, after review: testmaster_approve_healing or testmaster_reject_healing.

tools.name: mcp__testmaster__testmaster_review_plan
tools.description: Accept or reject proposals at expectedVersion = the batch version; an optional reason is kept. Returns acceptedProposals {proposalId, testId, revisionId}. Next: testmaster_run_tests.

expectedVersion.description: Batch version being reviewed, for optimistic concurrency

reason.description: Why you accept or reject; recorded on each decided proposal with the reviewer and time

tools.name: mcp__testmaster__testmaster_review_requirements
tools.description: Edit, adjudicate conflicts, reject (reason required; final) and approve requirements at snapshot expectedVersion, in that order; any list may be empty. Returns per-item results and sourceSnapshotId.

expectedVersion.description: Snapshot version these decisions are based on: version of testmaster_normalize_requirements or testmaster://requirements/{projectId}. Each item then applies at its requirement's current version

acceptanceCriteria.description: New acceptance criteria; replaces the list

update.description: Edits applied first; an edit clears the requirement's approval

selectedRequirementId.description: Requirement the conflict resolves to; the conflict's other requirements are superseded and never planned

adjudicate.description: Conflict decisions applied after the edits

requirementId.description: Requirement that is out of scope or not wanted

reason.description: Why it is rejected; required and recorded

reject.description: Rejections applied after the conflict decisions and before the approvals. A rejected requirement is not pending, is never planned and cannot be approved or edited again; an id in both reject and approve refuses the whole call

approve.description: Requirements to approve, applied last; a requirement in an unresolved conflict is refused

reason.description: Why you edit and approve; recorded on each edited or approved requirement with the reviewer and time (the requirements resource shows it). Rejections and conflict decisions carry their own reason

tools.name: mcp__testmaster__testmaster_rotate_secret
tools.description: Store a new value for an existing secret (id or name) from valueFile or fromEnv; the id, name and allowedOrigins stay, secretVersion goes up, and its users get the new value. Returns metadata only.

secret.description: Secret id (sec_...) or name of a live secret; its allowedOrigins and id stay, its secretVersion goes up

valueFile.description: File inside an approved root that holds the new value; one trailing newline is removed. Give exactly one of valueFile or fromEnv

fromEnv.description: Name of an environment variable of the TestMaster process that holds the new value. Give exactly one of valueFile or fromEnv

tools.name: mcp__testmaster__testmaster_run_tests
tools.description: Run testIds with environmentId, or a suite (suiteId, replay only), in the sandbox; revisionId pins one test's revision. Mode defaults to replay. wait=true blocks until timeoutMs (runs go on).

revisionId.description: Run this exact revision (candidate or healed) of the single test in testIds instead of its active one; not with suiteId

suiteId.description: List to run (replay only) instead of testIds

environmentId.description: Environment for testIds; lists carry their own

mode.description: replay (deterministic, default) or agent; lists run in replay only

confirmedExclusions.description: Lists only: exclusion keys accepted so the rest runs

stepTimeoutMs.description: Maximum ms for every step of this run: caps each step's own timeout and never lengthens it

jobId.description: Existing batch to re-read or wait on instead of admitting

idempotencyKey.description: 16-128 characters; a retried admission with the same key returns the same batch

timeoutMs.description: Wait deadline in ms, default 1800000 (30 min); runs continue after it

tools.name: mcp__testmaster__testmaster_save_auth_profile
tools.description: Create (projectId, name, kind, originBindings, secrets, config) or update (profileId, expectedVersion, fields) an auth profile; secrets are secret ids, username may be plain (unmasked).

projectId.description: Project id; required to create a profile

profileId.description: Profile to update; absent: create. Needs expectedVersion

expectedVersion.description: Current version of profileId, for optimistic concurrency

name.description: Profile name, unique in the project; required to create

kind.description: form, basic, bearer, api-key, cookie, oauth, oidc or manual; required to create, never changes

originBindings.description: Origins the profile may authenticate against; every environment that uses it must target one of them

secrets.description: Role to secret id (testmaster_set_secret): form password, totpSeed (username too when it is a secret); basic password; bearer token; api-key key; cookie cookie. Every role except username must be a secret; a plain value is refused

username.description: Username as a plain value (form, basic, oauth, oidc): stored and shown as written and NOT masked in evidence, so a username like root stays readable in DOM and logs. Use secrets.username instead to mask it (an e-mail, for example). Never both. On update, setting it replaces secrets.username

loginUrl.description: Login endpoint; its origin must be one of the profile's originBindings

contentType.description: Request body encoding: form (urlencoded) or json

fields.description: Request field names that receive the vault values (username, password, optional otp); never the values

staticFields.description: Constant extra request fields (for example a client id)

success.description: How a successful login is recognised and which credential it yields

statusIn.description: Response statuses that mean the login succeeded

cookieNames.description: Cookies kept as the session credential; omitted keeps every cookie set

tokenPointer.description: JSON pointer of a token in the response body, kept as the token credential

http.description: form: login by HTTP request; give exactly one of http and browser

browser.description: form: login in the browser; steps are plan action steps (contract PlanStep) that may reference this profile's secrets only; give exactly one of http and browser

challenge.description: form (optional) or manual (required): the human-only challenge and how it is resolved

otp.description: form or oauth/oidc: one-time-code settings; needs the totpSeed secret role

header.description: bearer, api-key or cookie: header or cookie the credential is meant for (documentation)

adapter.description: oauth/oidc (required): generic or cognito; cognito needs the cognito key

scopes.description: oauth/oidc (required): requested scopes; each must be in allowedScopes; oidc needs openid

allowedScopes.description: oauth/oidc (required): scopes the profile may ever request

redirectUri.description: oauth/oidc (required): the redirect URI in use; one of redirectUris

endpoints.description: oauth/oidc: explicit authorization, token, jwks and revocation endpoints

cognito.description: oauth/oidc with adapter cognito: region, endpoint and user pool

tokenScheme.description: oauth/oidc: prefix of the stored access token, default Bearer

ttlSeconds.description: manual: lifetime of the supplied session in seconds

config.description: Keys of the kind: form {http|browser}; basic, bearer, api-key, cookie: {} (header optional for the last three); oauth/oidc adapter, issuer, clientId, scopes, allowedScopes, redirectUris, redirectUri; manual challenge. Each key names its kinds

refreshPolicy.description: Session refresh limits; absent fields keep their defaults

tools.name: mcp__testmaster__testmaster_save_suite
tools.description: Create a test list, or change one at expectedVersion (selection, addMembers, removeMembers). Run it with testmaster_run_tests suiteId (replay only).

suiteId.description: Existing list to change; absent: create a list (name required)

expectedVersion.description: Current list version; required with suiteId

memberIntervalMs.description: Minimum ms between the starts of consecutive members of a batch of this list; 0 clears; absent keeps

selection.description: Whole selection: fixed pinned members or dynamic project filters. Create needs selection or addMembers; with suiteId it replaces the selection

addMembers.description: Fixed members (test, revision, environment) appended to the fixed selection, or the members of a new fixed list

removeMembers.description: Members to drop from a fixed selection; revisionId and environmentId narrow the match, absent they match every member of the test

tools.name: mcp__testmaster__testmaster_save_test
tools.description: Store a plan (ExecutablePlan, schema at testmaster://schemas/ExecutablePlan) as a new test (projectId) or a candidate revision of a test (testId); requirementRefs is required ([] if none). A new test is active at once; a candidate needs promotion.

plan.description: ExecutablePlan to store, linted like a CLI plan file. Schema: testmaster://schemas/ExecutablePlan (steps: testmaster://schemas/Step); check one with testmaster_validate_document

projectId.description: Create a new test in this project; give projectId or testId

testId.description: Add a new revision to this existing test instead; the revision is a candidate until testmaster_promote_revision

parentRevisionId.description: Revision the new one derives from; only with testId, must belong to that test

name.description: Test name for a new test; default: the plan name

justification.description: Why the test or revision is saved

tools.name: mcp__testmaster__testmaster_set_secret
tools.description: Register a secret from valueFile or fromEnv (never inline) with allowedOrigins; returns metadata only (locator = name). Taken name: testmaster_rotate_secret. Add secrets before plan generation.

name.description: Secret name: letters, digits, dot, underscore, hyphen; unique

valueFile.description: File inside an approved root that holds the value; one trailing newline is removed. Give exactly one of valueFile or fromEnv

fromEnv.description: Name of an environment variable of the TestMaster process that holds the value. Give exactly one of valueFile or fromEnv

allowedOrigins.description: Exact origins (scheme://host[:port]) the secret may be sent to; any other destination is refused

tools.name: mcp__testmaster__testmaster_test_auth_login
tools.description: Sign in once with an auth profile bound to an environment and report the outcome (authenticated, failed, blocked, checkpoint_required); saves nothing, never returns credentials. Scope X.

profileId.description: Auth profile to sign in with

environmentId.description: Environment the login targets; the profile must be bound to it (testmaster_update_environment authRefs)

tools.name: mcp__testmaster__testmaster_trial_plan
tools.description: Replay proposed plans of a batch against environmentId before review, with no model call; nothing is accepted. Returns per proposal the outcome, gate and the failed steps (expected, observed). Next: testmaster_edit_plan or testmaster_review_plan.

environmentId.description: Environment to replay the proposals' plans against

proposalIds.description: Proposals of the batch to try; absent: every proposal of the batch

tools.name: mcp__testmaster__testmaster_update_environment
tools.description: Change an environment at expectedVersion; give only the fields to change at top level (authRefs, additionalOrigins, ignoredOrigins, baseUrl, networkProfile, locale, timezone, production, name, serverLog).

expectedVersion.description: Current version of the environment, for optimistic concurrency

name.description: New name, unique in the project

baseUrl.description: New target URL of the application

additionalOrigins.description: Exact extra origins page subrequests may reach; replaces the list, [] clears it. They never receive credentials

ignoredOrigins.description: Exact origins whose requests are aborted and recorded without failing the run; replaces the list, [] clears it. Never reached

authRefs.description: Auth profiles bound to the environment; replaces the list. Each must be bound to the target origin

container.description: Docker container name or id (docker's name grammar)

serverLog.description: Opt-in docker container of the application server; its log lines during each attempt become logs/server.log. null stops reading it

tools.name: mcp__testmaster__testmaster_validate_document
tools.description: Validate an ExecutablePlan, ProjectConfig or RunRequest (schema names which) against its contract and plan rules; nothing is stored or run.

document.description: The document to validate; neither stored nor run. A plan's schema is the resource testmaster://schemas/ExecutablePlan

T0.description: The document to validate; neither stored nor run. A plan's schema is the resource testmaster://schemas/ExecutablePlan
